title: MAD-Max Beyond Single-Node: Enabling Large Machine Learning Model Acceleration on Distributed Systems
problem: Large-scale ML model training on distributed GPU clusters suffers from 14-32% of GPU hours spent on communication without computation overlap, creating significant latency bottlenecks and reducing overall efficiency.
motivation: Training and deploying large-scale machine learning models requires expensive distributed computing infrastructure and incurs substantial operational costs, making efficiency improvements critical.
method: MAD-Max is an agile performance modeling framework that analyzes real-world large model training on datacenter-scale GPU clusters to optimize parallelization strategies and identify hardware-software co-design opportunities by addressing communication latency and inefficiencies at scale.
key_novelty: A comprehensive performance modeling framework that jointly optimizes parallelization strategies and enables hardware-software co-design opportunities for distributed large-scale ML training.
contributions: Analysis revealing 14-32% of GPU hours wasted on non-overlapping communication in distributed ML training
MAD-Max performance modeling framework for optimizing parallelization strategies
Hardware-software co-design methodology for identifying optimization opportunities
Demonstrated throughput enhancements up to 2.24× for pretraining and 5.27× for inference on real models
limitations: Specific comparison baselines and hardware constraints not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: distributed ML acceleration via performance modeling
